# Accessibility conformance report

<!-- Generated by `node tools/conformance.mjs --write` from tools/conformance/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Product:** Gravitas 2.1.0  
**Standard:** WCAG 2.1 and 2.2, Levels A and AA  
**Date of evaluation:** 2026-10-17

## What this report is

This is The project's own evaluation. It is not an external audit, and no assistive-technology user has validated it (OWNER_ACTIONS.md lists the external work). It does not claim conformance. A criterion is reported **Supports** only when a method that can judge its whole scope covered the whole scope; a pass by axe-core alone is at most **Partially supports**, with the rules named. **Not evaluated** is used where no method here looked, which is neither a claim of support nor of failure. [ACCESSIBILITY.md](ACCESSIBILITY.md) says what was fixed and what cannot be; its list of honest limitations and this report must agree, and a test fails when they do not.

## Scope: the workflows evaluated

Ten student workflows and the instructor path, by the end-to-end specs that exercise them. Each is judged by the methods below on the surfaces and states those specs open.

| Workflow | What the student does | Specs |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Start from the front door and open an investigation | `onboarding.spec.js`, `firstRun.spec.js`, `investigations.spec.js` |
| S2 | Run and change a sandbox scenario | `sandbox.spec.js`, `bodyPlacement.spec.js`, `accessibilityParity.spec.js` |
| S3 | Work through an investigation: read, predict, answer, get feedback | `investigations.spec.js`, `answerEntry.spec.js`, `predictionLoops.spec.js` |
| S4 | Measure in an investigation and read a plot | `measure.spec.js`, `plotChart.spec.js`, `chartParity.spec.js` |
| S5 | Open an observation in the Observatory and measure it | `observatory.spec.js`, `stellarSpectra.spec.js` |
| S6 | Use the Sky Lab to plan an observation | `sky.spec.js`, `observing.spec.js` |
| S7 | Run an experiment and read its results | `experimentRunner.spec.js`, `experiments.spec.js` |
| S8 | Finish an investigation and download the report (PDF or web page) | `investigations.spec.js`, `htmlReport.spec.js` |
| S9 | Save, resume and export one's own work | `myWork.spec.js`, `progressSafety.spec.js`, `presetRecovery.spec.js` |
| S10 | Share a scenario by link and open a shared one | `sharing.spec.js`, `shareObserving.spec.js` |
| I1 | Find an investigation, assign it, collect submissions and review them | `adoption.spec.js`, `instructorFlow.spec.js`, `assignment.spec.js`, `submissionReview.spec.js`, `instructorPortal.spec.js` |

Outside the scope: Authoring tools (Scenario Studio, Investigation Composer, course builder) are covered by axe only (e2e/accessibility.spec.js); their workflows were not walked for this report. The generated PDFs are evaluated as documents, not as workflows.

## Methods

| Method | What it is, and what it cannot judge |
|---|---|
| **axe-core automated rules** (`axe`) | e2e/accessibility.spec.js runs axe-core with the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa and best-practice rule sets and no rules disabled, over every surface the spec lists, in both languages, and in all four themes on the pages that carry the shared shell. axe judges a subset of most criteria, reports some checks as incomplete (contrast over images, canvas and gradients), and cannot judge meaning, order or operation. |
| **Scripted manual checks** (`manual`) | e2e/accessibilityManual.spec.js: focus order, focus traps, Escape and focus restoration, heading order, landmarks, reflow at 320 and 640 CSS pixels, reduced motion and the canvas description. A scripted check judges what its assertions state, on the surfaces it opens. |
| **Keyboard and pointer parity** (`parity`) | e2e/accessibilityParity.spec.js and the dialog and body-placement specs: the keyboard and the typed form reach the same state as the pointer. |
| **The keyboard and single-pointer walks** (`walk`) | e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js (Prompt 278) presses real keys and makes single presses with no drag in a browser. It walks every page of the walk inventory (tools/interaction-contract.json, one row for each surface of the navigation inventory but the printed manual) in English and in Spanish: Tab from the top until focus comes round, then the page's primary control by its key. It also walks each control that replaces a drag. A walk judges the state a page opens in and the states it opens itself; it does not judge whether an order is meaningful, whether a focus indicator can be seen, or anything a screen reader says. |
| **Responsive layout and target size** (`layout`) | e2e/responsiveLayout.spec.js measures controls on phone and tablet projects, including the 44 px minimum on coarse pointers. |
| **Static inventories** (`static`) | tests/dialogInventory.test.js (every modal opens through js/dialog.js), tests/accessibilityDocs.test.js (every surface is named in the prose), tools/i18n-audit.mjs (both languages on every page) and the shell check (a language and a title on every stamped page). |
| **Inspection of the generated documents** (`pdf`) | tests/instructorMaterials.test.js holds the instructor PDFs to their stated untagged state; tests/evidenceLedger.test.js and tests/htmlReport.test.js check the tagged student report and the web-page report. No PDF/UA validator has been run. |
| **The structure, motion, reflow, forced-colors and target-size sweep** (`sweep2`) | e2e/a11ySweepII.spec.js (Prompt 279) and tests/motionInventory.test.js, in Chromium. Over the 32 pages of the walk inventory (the original-version page is exempt, with its reason): each page's outline against tools/page-outlines.json in English and in Spanish; one test for each focus pattern; the pages at rest with reduced motion, by the system and by the reader's setting; every page at 320 CSS pixels, and the Observatory and a lesson open; every page under forced colors; no checkbox or radio under 24 px. A scripted check judges what its assertions state on the pages and states it opens; it uses no assistive technology. |
| **The design ratchet's contrast record** (`ratchet`) | tools/design-ratchet.mjs measures the WCAG contrast ratio of 216 foreground and ground pairs of the design tokens in each of the four themes (text on the four surfaces; the accent, status colors and focus ring; a label on its button's face; the object hues on the sky), holds each to its minimum and to the recorded figure, so a ratio may only rise. It measures tokens, not what is drawn over a canvas, an image or a gradient. |

No method here is a test with assistive-technology users. **Assistive-technology user validation has not occurred**, so no criterion that depends on how a screen reader, switch or voice control behaves is reported as supported.

Every keyframes and scheduler in the sources is in tools/motion-inventory.json, and no page has a running animation or transition with reduced motion; four families of lesson instruments now start still under it. ## Stated gaps

From [ACCESSIBILITY.md](ACCESSIBILITY.md), "Honest limitations". Each is a limit no amount of ARIA removes; the criteria it touches are never reported as Supports.

| Limitation | Criteria |
|---|---|
| A sentence is not a simulation. | 1.1.1, 1.3.3 |
| The orbital motion itself does not stop for `prefers-reduced-motion`. | 2.2.2 |
| The shape of a curve is described by a template that no blind or low-vision reader has validated. | 1.1.1, 1.3.1 |
| Direct manipulation has a keyboard equivalent, but not a pointer's. | 2.5.1, 2.5.7 |
| The attribution links in the footer are under 24×24. | 2.5.8 |
| Automated checks are a floor, not a ceiling. | 1.3.1, 1.4.3, 4.1.2 |

## The generated documents

- **Instructor documents (PDF).** The instructor guides, answer keys, activity guides and worksheets are untagged PDFs (no /StructTreeRoot), so they are not PDF/UA conformant and give a screen reader no declared structure or reading order. The same content is on the web in HTML.
- **Student reports.** The student's lab report and evidence report are tagged PDFs (headings, lists, tables, figures with alternative text). No PDF/UA validator has been run on them, so their conformance is not claimed. The same report is offered as an accessible web page (Prompt 127).
- Affects criteria: 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 2.4.2, 3.1.1. For the untagged instructor PDFs those criteria are **Does not support**; the web pages that carry the same content are the route for a reader who needs structure.

## Updating this report

Edit tools/conformance/criteria.json (a status and its remarks) or product.json, then run `node tools/conformance.mjs --write`. A change to a status that makes a criterion Supports must name the method that judged its whole scope.
